head:
]executive Orber
Miss Ella Lee, of Mississippi, may be appointed to a clerical position
in the Postal Service, with a view to her appointment in the Post Office
at Jackson, Mississippi, without reference to the requirements of the civil
service rules.
Miss Lee is the daughter of the late Robert C. Lee, who for many
years was United States District Attorney for the Southern District of
Mississippi, and whose death about a year ago, together with the recent
death of her brother, renders it necessary for Miss Lee to secure employment
in order to provide a livelihood for herself and mother. It is stated that
Miss Lee is a graduate of the High School of Jackson, and well qualified
to fill a clerical position in the postal service; and that the postmaster will
appoint her to such a position if authorized to do so.
WOODROW WILSON
THE WHITE HOUSE,
28 April, 1916.
[No. 2371.]

Miss Emma B. Shreve and Miss Clara M. Tremper, wvho have been
employed temporarily in the office of the collector of customs at New York
in connection with the compilation of statistics through the installation of
accounting machines, may be permanently appointed' to clerical positions
in the Customs Service at New York without examiination under the civil
service rules.
The Acting Secretary of the Treasury states that the success of this
new system, which will result in a great saving of time and money, is
largely dependent upon the permanent at:pointment of these two women.
The accuracy of the government statistical reports depends upon the
accuracy of operations performed under the direction of Miss Shreve as
supervisor over about twelve young women operators. The collector of
customs at New York states that Miss Shreve has proven herself to be
especially capable and well fitted for this supervisory work.

the Underwood standard electrical adding and typewriting machine. The
tabulated reports as they come from the electrical machines are turned

priate articles, countries, etc., and transcribes this information in the form
of a typewritten report. This report is prepared upon wax sheets and any
errors therein would require it to be rewritten. Miss Tremper is one of
the speediest operators in the Unites. States, and the

head:
]executive Order
Civil Service Rule VII is hereby amended by adding at the end of
section 2 the following:
"and operatives, Office of the Auditor for the Post Office De-
partment, for the audit of accounts and vouchers of the postal service
by means of labor-saving devices; and operatives so appointed shall
not be eligible for transfer or promotion to apportioned positions or
for assignment to other workk"
The effect of this amendment will be to except from the requirement
of apportionment the operatives described, and to permit the holding of a
" local examination. The work of operatives is mechanical rather than
clerical, and to a great extent has been done by women employees in the
nonapportioned service, transferred from the Bureau of Engraving and
Printing under section 7 of Rule X. The Secretary of the Treasury states
that many persons appointed from the clerical registers of distant states in

head:
Executive rber.
It not infrequently happens that diplomatic and consular officers of the
United States are requested to be the medium of transmission of literary,
scientific or artistic works, or other gifts, which citizens or subjects of
foreign countries desire to present to the President.
In order that the practice in this regard may accord with that gener-
ally observed in the matter of similar presentations to the heads of other
governments, it is hereby ordered that diplomatic and consular officers of
the United States will hereafter, whenever request is made of them by a
citizen or subject of a foreign country to transmit a gift of any character
to the President, refuse to accept such gift and will advise the donor that
it is required that the presentation be made through the diplomatic repre-
sentative of the donor's government at Washington.
